# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Aug 17, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused heavily on CI/CD pipeline improvements, including optimizing merge queue test suites, enhancing release tag concurrency, and refining Rust CI workflows. Security updates for Go modules and toolchains were also implemented.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### CI/CD Pipeline Enhancements
Significant work was done to optimize and refine the CI/CD pipelines. This included skipping merge queue test suites for documentation-only changes to speed up the process [#22434](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22434). Additionally, each release tag was given its own APKO concurrency group to prevent bottlenecks [#22433](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22433), and Rust CI and prestate publishing workflows were configured to run correctly on the `develop` branch [#22421](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22421). Redundant protobuf apt packages were also removed from the `ci-base-clang` configuration [#22439](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22439), and Slack context was added to the `rust-nightly-bump` job for better notifications [#22438](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22438).

### Security Updates
Critical security updates were applied to Go dependencies. The `golang.org/x/mod` module was updated to version `v0.40.0` [#22425](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22425), and the Go toolchain directive was updated to `v1.26.6` [#22424](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22424).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
A number of new pull requests were opened, primarily focusing on dependency updates and CI/CD improvements. These include several `dependabot` PRs to bump Go modules such as `github.com/ipfs/go-ds-leveldb` [#22455](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22455), `github.com/hashicorp/go-hclog` [#22454](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22454), `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` [#22453](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22453), `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` [#22452](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22452), and `github.com/klauspost/compress` [#22451](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22451). Other new PRs address updating release documentation for `op-reth v2.4.2` and `op-contracts v8.0.0-rc.3` [#22448](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22448), removing an unused `ci-base-clang` Docker image [#22445](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22445), switching the Rust base image to a Wolfi runner image [#22444](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22444), validating dispute game configs in OPCM migrate [#22441](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22441), publishing a `-dev` image variant for APKO [#22440](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22440), and fixing the RPC effective gas price formula in `op-alloy` [#22437](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22437).

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES

### Unsafe Signer Rotation Handling Discrepancy
A new issue was opened regarding a difference in how `kona-node` and `op-node` handle unsafe signer rotation [#22447](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22447). The issue highlights that `op-node` allows a three-hour grace period for signer changes, while `kona-node`'s behavior is not explicitly defined, potentially leading to inconsistencies.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### SDM: Performance Benchmarking
The issue [#20176](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20176) concerning SDM performance benchmarking saw significant updates. The latest comments indicate that tracing on refund blocks is now working end-to-end in production, with `debug_traceBlockByNumber` succeeding on sampled sequencer blocks, including those with a trailing `0x7d`. No measurable latency penalty was observed for `0x7d` blocks. A full SDM A/B rerun confirmed earlier findings regarding gas savings and post-exec validation. CPU and RSS impact from SDM at 10-30 TPS loads were measured and found to be negligible. The final conclusion is that SDM shows no measurable overhead on `sdm-net-0` beyond a minor p99 PostExec delta under load. The issue is ready to be closed.
